headline: Manta Ray and Marine Conservation Regulations
reservation: State park entry for Kealakekua Bay and boat tours for Manta Ray encounters require separate independent bookings well in advance. Hulihe‘e Palace operates with specific tour times and may require online reservations. Always verify current DLNR rules for marine life interaction and reef-safe sunscreen requirements before arrival.

days.title: Kona Coast Heritage

stops.name: Pu‘uhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park
stops.detail: Walk the Great Wall and view the ti‘i (carved images) at this significant ancient place of refuge.

stops.name: Kealakekua Bay State Historical Park
stops.detail: View the Captain Cook Monument across the bay, a site of major historical contact and a protected marine sanctuary.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; traffic can slow near Captain Cook
days.note: Respect all sacred areas marked by 'kapu' signs; stay on established paths.

days.title: Coffee Belt and Cloud Forests

stops.name: Holualoa Village
stops.detail: Browse local art galleries and woodworking shops in this historic upland coffee-growing community.

stops.name: Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park
stops.detail: See ancient Hawaiian fishponds and petroglyphs carved into the lava rock near the shoreline.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; roads are narrow and winding in the uplands
days.note: Upland temperatures are significantly cooler than the coast; afternoon mist is common.

days.title: Kona Waterfront and Marine Life

stops.name: Kahalu’u Beach Park
stops.detail: Observe Hawaiian Green Sea Turtles in the shallow reef; please maintain a respectful distance from all wildlife.

stops.name: Mokua‘ikaua Church
stops.detail: Visit the oldest Christian church in Hawaii, constructed using lava rock and coral lime mortar.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local coastal transit
days.note: Beach parking fills rapidly; use local shuttles or arrive before the heat of the day.

intel.title: Beach Access
intel.text: Public parking at Kahalu’u is extremely limited and usually full by 9 AM. Small satellite lots exist along Ali'i Drive, but require a short walk to the main entry.

intel.title: Volcanic Shadows
intel.text: Cell reception is stable in Kailua-Kona but can drop significantly in the deep valleys of the South Kona district. Use GPS cautiously as older lava roads may not reflect current access.

intel.title: South Kona Services
intel.text: Fuel stations are frequent in Kailua-Kona but become sparse south of Captain Cook. Top off before heading to remote shorelines or the high-elevation coffee estates.

intel.title: Snorkel Visibility
intel.text: Morning hours offer the calmest water and best clarity for reef viewing before the afternoon trade winds pick up. Surface conditions can change rapidly in the afternoon.

intel.title: Historic Site Permits
intel.text: Access to specific archaeological sites at Kaloko-Honokōhau is pedestrian-only to protect sensitive resources. Check visitor center hours for access to the Honokōhau fishpond.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at KOA airport; the rental hub is a short shuttle ride from the open-air terminals. Stock up on supplies in Kailua-Kona before heading to resorts.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are sufficient for the Kona coast, though 4WD is required for specific high-mountain roads outside this itinerary; check rental restrictions for Saddle Road.
plan.goldenHour: Kailua Pier; arrive early to watch the sunset behind the horizon, keeping in mind the seasonal 'Vog' (volcanic haze) can intensify colors.
